glance: Anthropic's public IPO filing is the day's big story, putting hard numbers on revenue, compute spending and risk for the first time. Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro keeps pushing open-weight models toward the frontier. A quiet news window otherwise, so this edition is short.

stories.headline: Anthropic's public IPO filing reveals $16.3B half-year revenue and a compute bill measured in hundreds of billions
stories.why: The filing is the first detailed look at the economics of a frontier lab, and at how dependent AI products are on a few cloud and chip suppliers.
stories.source: Fortune · Axios · Motley Fool · SEC EDGAR
body: Anthropic has made its Form S-1 public, moving from a confidential draft filed in June to a document investors and customers can read in full. Press summaries of the filing put revenue for the first half of 2026 at about $16.3 billion, with roughly a fifth to a quarter coming from just two customers. Reports also cite a very large non-cash loss. Coverage differs on exact figures, so the SEC filing is the reference.

The compute numbers are the striking part. Outlets quote cloud commitments of around $450 billion over ten years, with total potential spending of $567 billion to $750 billion depending on how non-binding plans are counted. The filing reportedly says Anthropic has asked cloud partners for more capacity than they were willing to give, and that it plans to set up its own data centers. Power connections and permitting are named as the main data-center risks. The risk-factor section is long and includes warnings about extreme AI risks.

For product teams, the takeaway is dependency: model prices and availability rest on a handful of suppliers and on capital markets staying open. For automotive and industrial engineers using AI tools in simulation and validation, it is a reminder to avoid locking critical workflows to a single model provider.

stories.headline: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro lands near the top of independent rankings, with open weights promised by 4 November
stories.why: A cheap, open-weight model close to proprietary frontier systems gives European teams a self-hostable option for sensitive engineering data.
body: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro on Friday. It is a mixture-of-experts model with about 2.8 trillion total parameters, 104 billion active per token, and a one-million-token context window. The company says it will publish the full weights by 4 November.

Reports say API pricing is about $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Moonshot's headline result is 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, but that comes from the company's own testing and several comparison tests were built in-house. Artificial Analysis reportedly ranks the model fourth overall and first among open-weight models, still behind Anthropic's Opus 5.5. Moonshot itself says its offensive-cyber ability is below top proprietary models.

If the weights ship as promised, companies that cannot send design or test data to a US cloud could run a near-frontier model on their own hardware. Check the licence terms and run your own evaluations before relying on the vendor's benchmark figures.

watch.text: CleanTechnica reports Audi plans a roughly $4 billion plant in Georgia, with plug-in hybrids among the planned models. This is not yet confirmed by Audi in the material we found.

watch.text: Electrek relays reports that BYD may show an ultra-luxury EV with solid-state batteries in early November. The report relies on unnamed sources.
